multiplechoiceresponse.p: A user reports a slow computer. Which is the correct FIRST step?

choice.div: Gather information and identify the problem before changing anything.

div.p: Identify first. What changed, when, who is affected, and does it reproduce? Every later step depends on this.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A workstation shows signs of ransomware. The correct response is to:

choice.div: Isolate it and report through the incident channel.
Run a cleaner and keep working.

div.p: Isolate to stop the spread, preserve evidence, and escalate. Cleaning or deleting destroys evidence and may leave persistence behind.

choiceresponse.p: Which practices make a service desk healthy? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Writing knowledge-base articles for repeat problems
Working tickets by impact and urgency
Closing tickets without confirming the fix

div.p: Documentation, prioritisation, and communication are the backbone. Closing without confirmation is how reopen rates climb.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: You have spent your agreed window on a ticket with no progress. The professional move is to:

choice.div: Escalate with complete notes and an explicit ask.
Keep it forever so nobody else is bothered.

div.p: Escalation is a routing decision, not a failure. Hand over the evidence and what you need; do not sit on work that is beyond your scope.

choice.div: A signed certificate for the IT Support Capstone course, completing the IT Support Specialist track.
Nothing until you take an external exam.

div.p: A passing grade issues a course certificate automatically, signed through Signara. The track records the courses that together constitute the specialism.
